blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — piperacillin-tazobactam mechanism and antimicrobial stewardship
stem: A nurse is reviewing the pharmacology of piperacillin-tazobactam before administering it for a susceptible bacterial infection. Which statement about the combination is accurate?

options.A: Piperacillin inhibits bacterial septum formation and cell-wall synthesis, while tazobactam inhibits certain beta-lactamases that could otherwise inactivate beta-lactam therapy.
options.B: Tazobactam provides the main bactericidal activity by disrupting bacterial cell walls, while piperacillin chiefly slows renal elimination of the beta-lactamase inhibitor.
options.C: Piperacillin-tazobactam acts mainly by blocking bacterial protein synthesis at the ribosome, while tazobactam broadens activity by inhibiting microbial folate production.
options.D: Tazobactam neutralizes clinically important resistance mechanisms broadly enough that culture and susceptibility findings do not need to influence continued antibacterial therapy.

rationale: Current piperacillin-tazobactam labeling states that piperacillin exerts bactericidal activity by inhibiting septum formation and cell-wall synthesis of susceptible bacteria. Tazobactam has little clinically relevant antibacterial activity by itself but inhibits specified beta-lactamases. The label also directs clinicians to consider culture and susceptibility information when available when selecting or modifying antibacterial therapy. Therefore A is correct. B reverses the roles of the two components, C assigns unrelated antibacterial mechanisms, and D overstates the breadth of beta-lactamase inhibition and ignores susceptibility-guided therapy.
educational_objective: Describe piperacillin-tazobactam as a penicillin-class antibacterial plus beta-lactamase inhibitor and recognize that susceptibility information remains relevant when available.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine) / FDA labeling

source_claim_supported: Piperacillin provides bactericidal cell-wall synthesis inhibition, while tazobactam inhibits certain beta-lactamases; culture and susceptibility data should inform selection or modification of therapy when available.

candidate_reasons_resolved: Rewrote all four choices without absolute-word distractor cues.
Made each option a substantive antimicrobial-mechanism or stewardship statement of comparable length.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches current DailyMed mechanism and stewardship language. No absolute-word cue or second defensible answer remains.
